_doc: yf_price_bugfix.json  (configs/prices/)
Defects in YAHOO's own price data that no event feed can express, repaired at the point
`cube_part_prices` is built. Read by `StepCubePrices` via `level_basis.load_bugfix`.
## Why a register and not code
`level_factor` (S) undoes the spinoff adjustment Yahoo applied to `close_split`, and it
derives that adjustment from `prices_splits` -- Yahoo's own splits FEED. That works only
while the feed agrees with what Yahoo actually applied to the PRICES. Three ways it does
not, and none of them is inferable from the feed:
* SILENT ADJUSTMENT -- Yahoo back-adjusted the history and published no row at all.
IP's market cap reads 6.6% low for 20 years and `prices_splits` has no IP row.
* MIS-APPLIED ADJUSTMENT -- Yahoo published one factor and applied a different one on
a different date. JCI's `close_split` steps 70.354 -> 27.775 on 2007-07-02, a factor
of 0.3948, while its feed claims 0.25 and its REAL 3-for-1 was 2007-10-03 (where the
series does not step at all).
* SPLIT VINTAGE -- Yahoo adjusted PART of its own history for a split it published
and left the rest. MNST alternates between two bases inside three weeks.
Both are per-ticker facts about a vendor's data, established by measurement against an
independent source. That is a register, not an algorithm -- exactly like
`sharadar_corrections.json`, and for the same reason.
## Every entry states the DEFECT, not just the repair
⚠ This is the property that matters. An entry carries the value it EXPECTS to observe,
and `StepCubePrices` re-measures it on every build. If Yahoo fixes its data the
observation stops matching, the entry is SKIPPED and a warning is logged -- a stale
repair can never silently double-correct. Nothing here is applied on faith.
## `level_factor` -- a multiplicative LEVEL wedge
`factor` is the measured median of `sharadar_fundamentals.price / prices.close_split`
over the segment: multiply a LEVEL by it to reach the price the stock actually traded at.
It multiplies the computed `S`, so it lands in `cube_part_prices.level_factor` and every
market cap with it. ⚠ It NEVER touches a return -- see level_basis.py.
⚠ A SEGMENT IS A WINDOW `[previous before, this before)`, NOT a prefix, and its `factor`
is the WHOLE wedge for that era rather than an increment on the one before it. HBAN's
five eras measure 1.61051 / 1.46410 / 1.33100 / 1.21000 / 1.10005 and IP's two measure
1.07078 / 1.05600, each read off its own rows. Compounding them would put HBAN's 1995
bars at 4.17725, which is not a number anything measured; measuring them over an open
prefix reads the era BEFORE the one being checked, because the older rows outnumber the
newer ones and the median follows them.
`before` is EXCLUSIVE and is the corporate action's own date wherever one corroborates
the step. Two entries (BLDR, CCI) have no identified action; theirs sits at the midpoint
of the gap between the last bad filing and the first clean one, and says so.
Admission bar, applied when these were measured: at least 2 filing rows in the segment,
at most 0.5% spread WITHIN it, and at least 1% away from 1.0. ORCL, TMO and HAS were
measured and REJECTED by it -- their residuals are 1-row blips of 1-3%, not plateaus, and
encoding noise as a correction is worse than leaving it.
## `return_seams` -- a discontinuity that is not a price move
`step` is the observed one-bar ratio `close_split(d) / close_split(d-1)`. The bars BEFORE
`d` are multiplied by it, which makes the series continuous and removes the fabricated
return. Together with `split_vintage` this is one of the two repairs that change `ret`
and every label -- because a fabricated -61% return is a LABEL defect first and a level
defect second.
## Which LEGS a price repair moves
`close_split`, `close_total`, `open`, `high` and `low`, all by the SAME multiplier on the
same bar (`level_basis.REPAIRED_PRICE_FIELDS`). ⚠ The OHLC range is not optional: `_atr`
takes `high - low` and `high - close.shift(1)`, so repairing the close alone would not
merely leave those bars stale, it would make them INCOHERENT -- MNST would read a ~47
close inside a ~95 high/low band. Measured after the rebuild: 0 incoherent bars for MNST
and JCI, 1 in 3,262,477 universe-wide.
`volume` is deliberately NOT moved: MNST's two vintages show comparable volume (10.8M on
the last stale bar, 10.1M on the next adjusted one), so there is no measured defect, and
inventing a factor for a leg with no evidence is how a register starts lying. `ret` is not
moved either -- it is recomputed downstream FROM the repaired closes.
⚠ NOT a general de-spiking rule. A >40% one-bar move with no split on the books is
usually REAL: MO's 2008 Philip Morris International separation, AIG 2008-09-15, PCG's
2019 bankruptcy and the 2020-03-09 oil crash (APA/OXY/TRGP) all match that shape and all
happened. Only a move contradicted by an independent source belongs here.
## `split_vintage` -- a series left on TWO bases at once
The third and worst shape, and the reason this section exists at all. Yahoo publishes a
split, back-adjusts SOME of its own history for it, and leaves the rest alone. MNST's
2026-08-11 two-for-one is the case: five scattered bars in the three weeks before it are
adjusted and every other bar in thirty years is not, so the series alternates --
97.65, 48.19, 93.55, 47.08, 90.36, 45.53 -- with no market event anywhere near it.
⚠ Re-fetched LIVE from Yahoo on 2026-09-01, bar for bar. This is not a stale extract and
a full re-download does not touch it.
It cannot be a `factor`, because half the affected bars are already correct and halving
them would break them. So `ratio` is the split, and the repair anchors on the first bar
at or after `before` -- which is on the new basis BY DEFINITION, being the split itself --
and walks backwards, flipping a multiplier at every one-bar step that lands on the ratio
or its reciprocal. `expect_wedge` is what `sharadar.price / close_split` must still read
for the entry to fire, and the wedge is re-measured AFTER the walk to confirm it reached
1.0. Verified from both ends, refused from either.

_APPROVED.measured_by: scripts/spinoff_level_baseline.py + the segment scan in the plan
_APPROVED.note: Every `factor` is the measured median of sharadar.price / close_split over the segment, with spread <= 0.06% within each. Every `step` is the observed one-bar ratio in `prices`.

IP.evidence: Two spinoffs Yahoo back-adjusted the whole history for and published NO prices_splits row for. Returns around both dates are <3%, so the adjustment is smooth and correct FOR RETURNS -- it is only the LEVEL that is left short. 107 of 127 filing rows fail invariant 1 without this.

SJM.evidence: The 0.945 factor on 2002-05-30 IS in sharadar_actions and IS applied by Yahoo to prices, but it is a merger share-issuance factor, not a split, so `_is_split_shaped` rejects it (0.945 vs 17/18 = 5.6e-4) and it never reaches the denominator of S. 1/0.945 = 1.05820, which is the measured wedge to five decimal places.

HBAN.evidence: Five consecutive annual 10% STOCK DIVIDENDS. Each is genuinely split-shaped (11/10), so `split_events` keeps all five and they cancel out of S -- correctly, because they DO change the share count. But Sharadar's `price` does not reflect them while Yahoo's `close_split` does, so the level wedge is 1.1^n and compounds. The measured ladder reproduces 1.1^5..1.1^1 to five decimal places.

APA.evidence: The same stock-dividend mechanism as HBAN: a 10% (2001-12-27) and a 5% (2003-03-10), both split-shaped, both cancelling out of S, neither reflected in Sharadar's `price`. 1.1 x 1.05 = 1.155, which is the measured wedge exactly.

segments.event: 1.1 x 1.05 -- both stock dividends still ahead

HWM.evidence: Howmet's 2020 Arconic separation. Yahoo back-adjusted the history and published no prices_splits row. Corroborated by sharadar_actions 2020-04-01 spinoff of ARNC (value 0.25).

BX.evidence: Blackstone's PJT Partners separation. No prices_splits row; corroborated by sharadar_actions 2015-10-01 spinoff of PJT (value 0.025). A small wedge (1.9%) but a perfectly flat one across all 33 affected rows.

BLDR.evidence: A flat 18.9% wedge across all 18 pre-2010 filing rows, spread 0.00%. ⚠ NO corroborating corporate action was found in sharadar_actions -- the shape is unambiguous (a perfect plateau that ends), the CAUSE is not. Builders FirstSource ran a rights offering and a debt exchange through 2009-2010, either of which would do this.

segments.event: UNEXPLAINED -- boundary is the midpoint of 2009-10-28..2010-03-04

CCI.evidence: A flat 3.1% wedge across 17 filing rows to mid-2002, spread 0.04%. ⚠ NO corroborating corporate action found. Crown Castle restructured heavily in 2002. The single 2020-07-31 row at 0.97938 is NOT included -- one row is a blip, not a plateau.

segments.event: UNEXPLAINED -- boundary is the midpoint of 2002-05-14..2002-08-13

MNST.evidence: Yahoo back-adjusted FIVE bars for the 2026-08-11 two-for-one and left the other 7,793 alone. The five (2026-07-20, 07-21, 07-22, 07-31, 08-06) sit as islands inside the unadjusted run, so close_split reads 97.65 -> 48.19 -> 93.55 -> 47.08 -> 90.36 -> 45.53 with nothing in the market to explain it. The ten island edges are steps of 0.4895, 1.9559, 0.4935, 1.9413, 0.4984 and 1.9193 -- every one within 5% of 2.0 or 0.5, and the largest genuine MNST move in thirty years is +45.5%, so nothing real is near the flip band.
MNST.corroboration: sharadar.price / close_split is 0.50000 on all 122 filing rows from 1996-05-10 to 2026-08-07, flat to five decimals -- Sharadar carries the whole series on the post-split basis. Sharadar's 45.18 on 2026-08-07 equals 90.36 / 2 exactly. sharadar_actions has no MNST row after 2016-11-10, so the vendor's ACTION feed is stale even though its PRICE is right; the split is in prices_splits (2026-08-11, ratio 2.0), which is what `ratio` here refers to.
MNST.note: ⚠ The only entry that is direction-aware per bar, and the only one that is NOT a stale-extract artifact -- re-fetched live from Yahoo on 2026-09-01 and reproduced exactly. Volume is deliberately left alone: 10.8M on the last stale bar against 10.1M on the next adjusted one is no evidence of a re-basing, and inventing a factor for a leg with no measured defect is how a register starts lying.

JCI.evidence: close_split falls 70.354 -> 27.775 in one bar, a -60.52% return that never happened. JCI's real 3-for-1 was 2007-10-03, where the series does NOT step. yfinance's own feed claims 0.25 on this date; the applied factor is 0.3948. So the feed, the applied adjustment and the real event disagree three ways, and the bar is corroborated by NOTHING -- Sharadar's price shows no such move.
JCI.note: ⚠ This repairs the fabricated RETURN, which is what reaches momentum, vol, betas and every JCI label. It does NOT make JCI's level basis correct: the residual wedge drifts monotonically across 83 segments (0.32 -> 0.11 over 1996-1999), which is a corrupt series rather than a basis offset and cannot be expressed as a factor. MNST's defect looked like this one and turned out NOT to be -- see split_vintage -- so JCI stays the last named residual, and it is the genuinely corrupt one.
